correctness.rationale: The quadratic cell minimum formula is proved from nearest half-integral lattice centers, with periodicity, half-period symmetry, breakpoint ties and scale invariance covered. All C(31,8)=7,888,725 nondecreasing height-24 eight-tuples are evaluated in exact integer arithmetic. The accompanying C++ source enumerates all tuples without omissions and compares rational values with 128-bit cross-products; maxima are exactly the primitive vector (1,2,3,4,5,7,9,11) and its double, both 8/17. The independent Fraction checker confirms the hero, all height-7 tuples and 300 additional deterministic samples. Explicit 16-cell numerator list verifies 8/17 independently. This is finite completeness for height<=24, not an unrestricted D8 certificate.

originality.rationale: The motivating manuscript settles the unrestricted constants for dimensions six and seven, and explicitly asks for a dimension-eight candidate. Its exact per-direction evaluator is background, but its published results do not give the new exhaustive height-24 eight-dimensional maximum or equality set. No equivalent or dominating statement appeared in four targeted scientific-record searches, exact vector and alternate-normalization scientific searches, or inspected relevant primary full texts. The related 2016 zonotope paper addresses mainly cube norm obstruction. Historical-priority risk remains.
residual_risks: Historical priority is not certified: an earlier unpublished or poorly indexed eight-dimensional finite direction census may exist.
The 2016 full text was sampled at its relevant principal definitions and equivalences rather than every appendix; the 1996 historical article was only available in abstract form.
The unrestricted eight-dimensional maximum may be strictly larger; no finite bound on coordinates of a global extremizer is proved.
The finite classification is a self-contained same-model-reviewed computational proof, not an independent mathematical audit.
